title: Turkey, squash and black bean stew

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain tin or stock, with nothing factory-built like a jar sauce or stock pot.

supermarket.reason: Turkey mince, butternut squash, tinned black beans and Greek yoghurt are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a casserole, a wooden spoon and a knife, and the technique is simple frying and simmering.

works.reason: The quantities make a generous pot for four, the tomato and stock liquid suits a covered simmer, and 2cm squash cubes will be tender in 25 minutes.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of active work covers peeling and cubing a squash, chopping an onion and 8 minutes of browning, and the 25-minute cook matches the simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming squash stew suits early February, and the squash is a main body of the dish, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family stew of lean meat, beans and vegetables.
